service.description: Dispatch one MCP JSON-RPC request through the conformance gates, resolve the method via the allowlist map, and wrap the outcome in the JSON-RPC envelope. The screen passes the transport facts (headers, parse state) as plain parameters, which is what keeps every gate testable at the service level; httpStatus is returned for tests and applied to the real response by the transport screen. Anonymous callers reach discover/list only; exec#Tool gates actual tool runs on a real user until the OAuth resource-server step.

parameter.name: id
parameter.description: JSON-RPC id, echoed verbatim (string or number, so Object). Absent means the message is a notification.

parameter.name: parseError
parameter.description: Body JSON parse error text, when parsing failed.

parameter.name: response
parameter.description: The JSON-RPC response body; null for a notification (202, no body).

service.description: The MCP tool catalog: scan every component's service directory for *.mcp.xml files (the source is fixed, exactly like RestApi's *.rest.xml scan; no in-parameters, so nothing a caller sends can point it at a file) and cache the result. The ai.mcp.tool.catalog cache is declared in MoquiConf.xml with no expiry; a rebuild happens on any cache miss.

parameter.name: toolList
parameter.description: Sorted by tool name. Each: name, title, description, serviceName, inputSchema, outputSchema, fixedParameters, annotations. NOTE: callers share the cached object graph — read only, never mutate.

service.description: Pure transformer: parse the given *.mcp.xml file locations and apply the scan rules (documented in BuildToolCatalog.groovy). No cache, no default source. Separate from get#ToolCatalog so the rules are testable against fixture files without giving the cached endpoint path any way to name a file.

Execute a resolved catalog tool definition with the given arguments and return the MCP CallToolResult body (content, structuredContent, isError). Internal: called by call#Tools with a catalog entry, and by tests with a build#ToolCatalog entry. Requires a real (non-anonymous) user and runs as them; the backing service's own authenticate and authz decide what they may do. Failures become isError:true text, never an exception on the wire.
